title: a pipeline whose reader exits early is unsound under pipefail
body:
# 0031: a pipeline whose reader exits early is unsound under pipefail

## Tags

pipefail, sigpipe, false-green, flaky, doctor, ci, gates

## Summary

`grep -q` returns the instant it matches. `head -n1` returns after one line. Either one leaves the writer on the left of the pipe holding a `write()` that will never be read, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and **`set -o pipefail` promotes that 141 to the exit status of the whole pipeline** -- which the surrounding `&&`, `if` or `set -e` then reads as the answer to the question being asked.

Every affected site in this project sets `set -euo pipefail`. Four sites, three distinct consequences, all silent -- and **the rule is not "a reader that exits early", which cost one wrong row in the first version of this table** (see Refuted, below):

| Site                    | Shape (`->` is a pipe)                | What the promotion does                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `lib/cmd/doctor:196`    | `printf "$states" -> grep -q "$rel$"` | an OWNED file is reported unowned -- a wrong diagnosis       |
| `lib/cmd/new:131`       | `find -> sort -> head -n1`            | `set -e` aborts `devbin new` instead of `return 1`           |
| `lib/cmd/check:402`     | `find -> head -1`                     | `set -e` aborts the version gate mid-check                   |
| `.github/workflows:100` | `printf -> grep -q`                   | last command of a gate step -- a lost race fails CI outright |

**The bug is on the MATCH path.** The miss path -- where the reader consumes to EOF -- is the one that always worked, so every one of these behaves correctly on the case that finds nothing and misbehaves on the case that finds something.

## Reproduction

Found as an intermittent CI failure: run 32787816443, `Test on macOS (bash >= 5 floor)`, one test red out of 649 --

```
not ok 427 R5: a clean install reports nothing unowned
  `refute_output_contains "unowned"' failed
  .../lib/cmd/doctor: line 196: printf: Broken pipe
  .../lib/cmd/doctor: line 196: printf: write error: Broken pipe
    note  unowned files under bin/.devbin/lib
          bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/install
  ok    manifest: 28 vendored files intact
  9 checks, 0 failed, 3 notes
```

`bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/install` is entry 28 of 28 in that manifest and was verified intact one line above. The commit under test changed a single whiteboard file, and the previous run on the same code was green.

The mechanism, isolated -- twenty iterations of the doctor line, identical input, pipefail the only variable:

```
pipefail ON : matched=0   reported-unowned=20
pipefail OFF: matched=20  reported-unowned=0
```

And the `lib/cmd/new` shape, over a tree with 4000 `.bats` files:

```
lib/cmd/new shape: FAILED, status 141 -- devbin new would abort here
```

## Root Cause

`pipefail` exists so a failing producer is not hidden by a succeeding consumer. SIGPIPE is the one case where the producer's non-zero status carries no information about the producer: it is the *consumer* saying "I have enough". `pipefail` cannot tell those apart, so a deliberate early exit is indistinguishable from a real upstream failure.

**There are two loss modes, and only one of them is bounded by payload size.** The distinction matters because the obvious analysis finds the bounded one, concludes the defect needs an implausible input, and files it as theoretical.

- **Buffer-blocking, deterministic-ish.** Once the payload is large enough, `printf` blocks mid-write and `grep`'s early exit strands it every time. **There is no single threshold, and the first version of this entry claimed one.** It read "a sharp cliff at exactly 64K -- `lost=0/20` at 64599, `lost=20/20` at 66299", which was a true measurement at one line width and false as a general statement. Holding bytes constant at 60000 and varying only the width:

| line width | lines | bytes | lost |
| ---------- | ----- | ----- | ---- |
| 6          | 10000 | 59999 | 7/20 |
| 18         | 3333  | 59993 | 2/20 |
| 60         | 1000  | 59999 | 0/20 |
| 200        | 300   | 59999 | 0/20 |
| 600        | 100   | 59999 | 0/20 |

  Same bytes, 7/20 to 0/20 on shape alone. intent/vc measured onset between 40K and 60K where this machine measured 64.6K-66.3K, and the difference was METHOD, not machine -- their padding sat at the narrow end. **So "we are under the limit" is not a defence, because there is no portable limit to be under.** This is the mode the regression test forces, which is why the test pads well past any observed onset rather than to a computed one.
- **Scheduling, probabilistic, at ANY size.** `printf` runs in a forked subshell; if that fork is preempted between `fork()` and its `write()` while `grep` runs to completion and exits, the write lands on a closed pipe. No blocking, no buffer involved, no size threshold. Measured at the payload size devbin actually had -- 839 bytes, 28 entries, match on line 1, twelve spinning processes for load: **`lost=1/6000`**.

The CI failure was the second mode, and the output says so: **exactly one file of 27 was flagged, not all of them.** Buffer-blocking would have flagged every one, which is what the unfixed code does under the regression test. A single flagged file is a single unlucky interleaving.

So payload size does not bound reachability, and a "this would need N thousand entries" argument against the finding is measuring the wrong mode. What raises the probability is load, which is what CI is.

A second, pre-existing defect died with the same line: `grep -q "<TAB>$rel$"` interpolates a path into a **regular expression**, so `.` in a vendored filename matched any character. A stray file named `helper.` would have matched the owned entry `helpers` and been reported as owned. Exact string comparison has no such hole.

## Impact

`doctor` is the tool a project runs to be told its install is sound, so a wrong answer there is worth more than the same wrong answer anywhere else -- and the failure direction is toward accusing a clean install, not toward excusing a dirty one, which is the better of the two but still a wrong diagnosis printed with full confidence.

`devbin new` and `lib/cmd/check` are the loud ones, and they are worse than probabilistic: there `head` is the READER, so on `find | sort | head -n1` the reader decides after 1 line of 100000 and the rest is stranded every time. Driven by devbin/cc at 200/200 on a tree of any size -- not a race at all.

## Proposed Fix

Remove the pipeline wherever the reader can exit early. Not `|| true`, which would suppress genuine writer failures along with the spurious ones.

- `lib/cmd/doctor` -- extract the owned set once with `cut` (which reads to EOF, so there is no early exit to race), then test membership with the existing public `list_contains`. That helper is documented as public precisely so a third spelling of "is this path in that set" does not appear; this is the second caller it was written for. Fewer forks than the version it replaces, and exact string equality rather than a regex.
- `lib/cmd/new`, `lib/cmd/check` -- let the producer finish into the command substitution, then take the first line in bash with `${f%%$'\n'*}`.
- The workflow -- drop the trailing `printf | grep -q` at `:100` for a here-string. **That is the only workflow change**; the collector was reverted, see below.

### Visited and excluded, with the reason -- these are NOT unvisited

Naming them, because "we did not look there" and "we looked and it is fine" must not be the same silence, and because as the first version of this table stood each of these reads as an oversight someone should go and fix.

- **`.github/workflows/tests.yml:149` (`head -n1 "$s" | grep -qE`) -- SOUND.** `head -n1` writes exactly one line and grep is line-oriented, so grep cannot decide until it holds a complete line: its decision point is at or after the writer's last byte and there is no unread remainder to strand. This issue first claimed the opposite and a fix was written and then **reverted**. A comment now sits above the line saying not to fix it.
- **`bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate:58` -- SOUND, same shape, and it is wired as three live gates** (`config.yaml:60,65,81` -- syntax, lint, critic). Found by devbin/cc going looking for a fifth site this issue had missed. It is not one. Left alone.
- **`.github/workflows/tests.yml:84-85` (`$(bash --version | head -1)`) -- no defect.** The substitution captures line 1 whatever happens next, and its status is discarded because it is an argument rather than a command.
- **`lib/cmd/check:386` (`elixir --version | awk '/^Elixir / {print $2; exit}'`) -- sound, but by ORDERING not by structure.** awk exits after the Elixir line, which is last, so nothing is stranded. Recorded because it would stop being sound if the tool ever reordered its output. Not filed.

### Refuted: one row of the original table was wrong

The first version of this issue attributed "a file is dropped from the lint set while the job still prints ShellCheck clean" to `head -n1 | grep -qE`. **That is false and it was measured false**, by devbin/cc first and then independently here. The isolation is the cheapest possible -- equal bytes, match at byte 0, one variable:

| payload       | bytes  | lost    |
| ------------- | ------ | ------- |
| ONE long line | 200007 | 0/200   |
| MANY lines    | 216007 | 200/200 |

And under load, 6000 iterations, with a positive control in the same run that did lose:

| shape (`->` is a pipe)                               | lost   |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `head -n1 -> grep -qE` (1 line, reader needs it all) | 0/6000 |
| `printf` 28 lines `-> grep -qxF` (27 stranded)       | 1/6000 |

The zero is only meaningful because the control is not zero. **So the rule is: unsound when the reader can DECIDE before consuming everything the writer will write** -- which coincides with "exits early" in three of the four sites here and comes apart in exactly the fourth. Stated loosely it would have sent the next reader to churn three live gates for no defect, and this issue's own near-miss below is the measured cost of churning sound code.

## Verification

The existing `R5: a clean install reports nothing unowned` cannot be the regression test: it is the test that was green all along. A second test pads the manifest with genuinely owned files -- real files, real checksums, appended to the manifest -- until the states block clears a 64K pipe buffer, which forces `printf` to block and makes `grep`'s early exit strand it every time. It asserts the same invariant, not the padding.

Driven red against the unfixed `lib/cmd/doctor` first, where it reported **every** vendored file as unowned. Green after. The test also asserts its own padding clears 64K, so a later change that shrinks it cannot quietly turn it back into a coin flip.

**One near-miss worth recording, because it was the same defect coming back in through the patch.** The workflow fix first read the shebang as `IFS= read -r shebang <"$s" || shebang=""`. `read` returns 1 at EOF *after* assigning, so any shell file whose last line lacks a trailing newline would have had its `#!/bin/bash` cleared and been dropped from the lint set -- silently, which is precisely the behaviour being fixed. Caught by reading the patch rather than by any check, since the repository has no such file today and no test would have gone red. `|| true` keeps what was read.

## Devbin's own exposure, measured

The same class lives in Intent's shipped whiteboard guards (`whiteboard-clock-guard.sh:246`, `whiteboard-header-guard.sh:201`, both under `set -uo pipefail`), where the pipeline is the "did THIS COMMIT add it" filter -- so a lost race calls a real violation inherited and passes the commit. Issue 0030 is about arming those guards here, so devbin's own numbers decide whether arming is a good trade:

- Worst real board payload across all devbin history: **13374 bytes, 70 lines, mean width 191** (commit 01637c0).
- Driven verbatim at that exact payload and shape, 200 iterations: **lost=0/200**.
- The same payload at 5x (66869 bytes, same shape): **lost=197/200**.

So devbin has roughly 5x headroom on the deterministic mode at its current board shape, and is exposed only to the scheduling mode. **Arming the guards remains net-positive** -- an unsound guard beats the nothing devbin has now -- but "armed" must not be read as "sound", and the stripped-`Z` red-drive exercises check B, which is syntactic and has no pipeline.

Credit where it is owed: intent/vc drove this rather than relaying it, caught that the repro handed to them under-reproduced, and split one finding into two severities by measuring that the two guards' payloads differ by three orders of magnitude (deduped stamps vs every added line, full text).

## Related

- `intent/llm/LESSONS.md` -- "The machine underneath"; and intent/dc's entry on defects that return the correct answer on the case in front of you. This one is the harder variant: it returns the correct answer on *most executions of the same case*.
- 0025 -- the other finding whose fix had to be checked against everything downstream of it

## Resolutions

Fixed in all four sites, with a red-first regression test for the one that reached CI.
